name: The flattest stretch of P&L
brief:
`pnl` is a desk's daily P&L in pounds, a non-empty list of whole numbers. A stretch is one or more consecutive days. Return the smallest absolute total of any stretch, so 0 when some stretch nets to exactly £0.

Write `flattest_stretch(pnl)`.

Example. For `[10, -3, -4, 9]` the stretch of the last three days totals 2. No stretch is closer to zero, so the answer is 2.
constraints: $O(n \log n)$ time is the target. Trying every start and end day is too slow.
All tests share a 5-second time limit.
hint: A stretch total is the difference of two prefix totals. Which two prefix totals are closest together, and where do they sit once the list of them is sorted?

examples.note: The first three days net to exactly £0.

tests.call: flattest_stretch([((i * 7919) % 100003) * (1 if i % 2 else -1) * 1000 + 1 for i in range(1, 100001)])

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Each stretch total is `pre[j] - pre[i]`, and the closest pair of prefix totals sits side by side once sorted.
Taking the smallest single day misses stretches like -3, -4, 9, whose total beats every day alone.
Building `pre` is $O(n)$ and sorting it is $O(n \log n)$.
